target_customer: Adults in queer, polyamorous and alternative communities who want to meet people through events, plus event organizers
problem: Alternative communities find it hard to meet friends and partners safely and organically outside swipe-based dating apps.
business_model: Freemium consumer app with paid Plura+ tier, partnering with event producers
product_category: Social and dating community around in-person events

founders.name: Lauren (Luna) Ray Vegter
prior_employers: Facebook (about 5 years, led Instagram user growth)
education: MIT, degrees in business and engineering
founders.background_notes: YC says she replaced herself as CEO and now coaches founders; date not given. Growth figures for Instagram differ between bios.

technical_complexity.rationale: A mobile social app with event listings and chat is standard engineering; trust and moderation are the hard parts.

defensibility.rationale: Local event communities and referral based membership create local network effects, though events can move to other platforms.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying the model; Feeld runs its own in person events today.

market_need_then: Nonmonogamous and queer communities were underserved by mainstream dating apps, and event-based meeting was a stated gap. No dated 2020 usage data was sourced.

branding.name_origin: A secondary directory says Plura reflects the plural nature of identity and belonging; unverified.
branding.domain_note: Uses heyplura.com; the app bundle id still reads community.together.bloom.

identity.logo: Bloom logo file name remains on the site
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm, inclusive, playful, describing itself as a queer and woman-led company

branding.brand_signature: Consent culture and referral based membership

rebrands.why: Unverified secondary source says to reflect plurality; CB Insights also lists an earlier name Together.

branding.community_and_virality: Business Insider covered Bloom's pitch deck in September 2022 per a link on the YC page; article not read.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear community positioning and some press, but the rename away from Bloom and a niche focus limit reach.

outcome_analysis: Bloom Community raised a 2.5M seed in September 2022, launched city by city, and later became Plura, with the founder moving from CEO to chair. The company is active with five staff. No later round, exit, or traction number was found, so the story is unresolved and the niche audience is the main constraint.
notes: Seed confirmed by PR Newswire and Pulse 2.0. Totals conflict (2.5M, 2.65M, CB Insights 500K) and one source calls the round Series A. Rebrand date and reason not found. YC page lists Oakland and San Diego. Competitor search returned only current Feeld material, so the list is empty. Outcome search found no shutdown or acquisition.
